stops.note: the princess-abbess who founded Ely Abbey in 673; Bede says she died of a neck tumour she took as punishment for wearing necklaces in her youth
Norman-era Audrey replaced the Old English name; at Ely's St Audrey's fair, silk neck-laces called 'St Audrey's lace' were sold in her memory
'tawdry lace' ran together from 'St Audrey', and the cheap fair-goods gave the word its sense of showy but worthless

current_meaning: showy but cheap and of poor quality
